75222-the-draycott-murder-mystery.creator: Molly Thynne
75222-the-draycott-murder-mystery.description: A book by Molly Thynne. The sun had set and it was already dark when the first sound of footsteps was heard in the lane. The walker approached quickly, with an odd, shuffling tread that became almost noiseless as he neared the house.

arxiv-2101-06656.title: On the simultaneous recovery of the conductivity and the nonlinear reaction term in a parabolic equation Thanks: The first author is supported by FWF grant P30054; the second author is supported by NFS grant dms -1620138 Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author: William Rundell
arxiv-2101-06656.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . This paper considers the inverse problem of recovering both the unknown, spatially-dependent conductivity a ⁡ ( x ) a(x) and the nonlinear reaction term f ⁡ ( u ) f(u) in a reaction-diffusion equation from overposed data. These measurements can consist of: the value of two different solution measurements taken at a later time T T ; time-trace profiles from two solutions; or both final time and time-trace measurements from a single forwards solve data run.

arxiv-2108-06671.title: An observable for the separation distance of two photons
arxiv-2108-06671.creator: Scott E. Hoffmann
arxiv-2108-06671.description: Abstract Motivated by an intention to apply partial wave analysis to systems containing photons, we construct eigenvectors of the distance of separation between two photons. A choice is made that makes the case of two photons most closely resemble the case of two massive particles. The treatment is relativistic.

arxiv-2110-03510.title: Probing Light Mediators in the Radiative Emission of Neutrino Pair
arxiv-2110-03510.creator: Shao-Feng Ge, Pedro Pasquini
arxiv-2110-03510.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shao-Feng Ge, Pedro Pasquini. We propose a new possibility of using the coherently enhanced neutrino pair emission to probe light-mediator interactions between electron and neutrinos. With typical momentum transfer at the atomic 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 CLOSE \mathcal{O}(1 eV) scale, this process is extremely sensitive for the mediator mass range 𝒪 ⁡ ( 10 − 3 ∼ 10 4 CLOSE \mathcal{O}(10^{-3}\sim 10^{4} ) eV.

arxiv-2207-01942.title: An Exploratory Study on Regression Vulnerabilities CCS: Security and privacy Software security engineering CCS: Software and its engineering Software testing and debugging
arxiv-2207-01942.creator: Larissa Braz, Enrico Fregnan, Vivek Arora, Alberto Bacchelli
arxiv-2207-01942.description: Abstract . Background: Security regressions are vulnerabilities introduced in a previously unaffected software system. They often happen as a result of source code changes ( e.g., a bug fix) and can have severe effects. Aims: To increase the understanding of security regressions. This is an important step in developing secure software engineering.

arxiv-2210-04835.title: Factoring numbers with elliptic curves
arxiv-2210-04835.creator: Jorge Jiménez Urroz, Jacek Pomykała
arxiv-2210-04835.description: Abstract . In the present paper we provide a probabilistic polynomial time algorithm that reduces the complete factorization of any squarefree integer n n to counting points on elliptic curves modulo n n , succeeding with probability 1 − ε 1-\varepsilon , for any ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 . 1.

arxiv-2301-05516.title: CLT for real β \beta -ensembles at high temperature Thanks: This project has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union Horizon 2020 research and innovation program (grant agreement No. 884584).
arxiv-2301-05516.creator: Charlie Dworaczek Guera, Ronan Memin
arxiv-2301-05516.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Charlie Dworaczek Guera, Ronan Memin. We establish a central limit theorem for the fluctuations of the linear statistics in the β \beta -ensemble of dimension N N at a temperature proportional to N N and with confining smooth potential. In this regime, the particles do not accumulate in a compact set as in the fixed β > 0 \beta>0 case which results in an equilibrium measure supported on the whole real line.

arxiv-2306-16605.title: KITE: Keypoint-Conditioned Policies for Semantic Manipulation
arxiv-2306-16605.creator: Priya Sundaresan, Suneel Belkhale, Dorsa Sadigh, Jeannette Bohg
arxiv-2306-16605.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Priya Sundaresan, Suneel Belkhale, Dorsa Sadigh, Jeannette Bohg. While natural language offers a convenient shared interface for humans and robots, enabling robots to interpret and follow language commands remains a longstanding challenge in manipulation.

arxiv-2402-17861.title: Towards AI Accountability Infrastructure: Gaps and Opportunities in AI Audit Tooling Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26-May 1, 2025, Yokohama, Japan DOI: 10.1
arxiv-2402-17861.creator: Victor Ojewale, Ryan Steed, Briana Vecchione, Abeba Birhane, Inioluwa Deborah Raji
arxiv-2402-17861.description: Abstract . Audits are critical mechanisms for identifying the risks and limitations of deployed artificial intelligence (AI) systems. However, the effective execution of AI audits remains incredibly difficult, and practitioners often need to make use of various tools to support their efforts.

arxiv-2410-09144.title: Auriga Streams I: disrupting satellites surrounding Milky Way-mass haloes at multiple resolutions
arxiv-2410-09144.creator: Alexander H. Riley, Nora Shipp, Christine M. Simpson, Rebekka Bieri, Azadeh Fattahi, Shaun T. Brown, Kyle A. Oman, Francesca Fragkoudi, Facundo A. Gómez, Robert J. J. Grand, and Federico Marinacci
arxiv-2410-09144.description: Abstract In a hierarchically formed Universe, galaxies accrete smaller systems that tidally disrupt as they evolve in the host’s potential. We present a complete catalogue of disrupting galaxies accreted onto Milky Way-mass haloes from the Auriga suite of cosmological magnetohydrodynamic zoom-in simulations.

arxiv-2503-22014.title: Ground states of quasi- two-dimensional correlated systems via energy expansion
arxiv-2503-22014.creator: Sam Mardazad, Nicolas Laflorencie, Johannes Motruk, Adrian Kantian
arxiv-2503-22014.description: Abstract We introduce a generic method for computing groundstates that is applicable to a wide range of spatially anisotropic 2D many-body quantum systems. By representing the 2D system using a low-energy 1D basis set, we obtain an effective 1D Hamiltonian that only has quasi-local interactions, at the price of a large local Hilbert space.

arxiv-2503-23286.title: Diophantine approximation of multiple zeta-star values
arxiv-2503-23286.creator: Jiangtao Li
arxiv-2503-23286.description: Abstract . The set of multiple zeta-star values is a countable dense subset of the half line ( 1 , + ∞ ) (1,+\infty) . In this paper, we establish some classical Diophantine type results for the set of multiple zeta-star values. Firstly, we give a criterion to determine whether a number is a multiple zeta-star value.

arxiv-2507-18910.title: A Systematic Review of Key Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems: Progress, Gaps, and Future Directions
arxiv-2507-18910.creator: Agada Joseph Oche, Ademola Glory Folashade, Tirthankar Ghosal, Arpan Biswas
arxiv-2507-18910.description: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) represents a major advancement in natural language processing (NLP), combining large language models (LLMs) with information retrieval systems to enhance factual grounding, accuracy, and contextual relevance. This paper presents a comprehensive systematic review of RAG, tracing its evolution from early developments in open-domain question answering to recent state-of-the-art implementations across diverse applications.

arxiv-2601-03861.title: Short gamma-ray burst progenitors have short delay times
arxiv-2601-03861.creator: M. Pracchia, O. S. Salafia
arxiv-2601-03861.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by M. Pracchia, O. S. Salafia. Short gamma-ray bursts (SGRBs) are thought to be primarily associated with binary neutron star (BNS) mergers. The SGRB population can therefore be scrutinized for signatures of the delay time between the formation of the progenitor massive star binary and the eventual merger, which could produce an evolution of the cosmic rate density of such events whose shape departs from that of the cosmic star formation history.

pmc-10573552.creator: Camila Patricio Braga Filgueira, Daniela Pitta-Pereira, Lilian Motta Cantanhêde, Gabriel Eduardo Melim Ferreira, Sayonara Dos Reis, Elisa Cupolillo, Otacilio C. Moreira, Constança Britto, Mariana Côrtes Boité
pmc-10573552.description: High Resolution Melting Analysis (HRM) has been pointed out as a suitable alternative method to detect and identify Leishmania species. Herein, we aimed to evaluate the sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and limitations of a HSP70-HRM protocol both as a diagnostic scheme applied in clinical samples and as a species typing tool for laboratory research and reference services.

pmc-11516682.creator: H Muelas, J Quiles, A Boned-Ombuena, P Vicent, P Hernández, P Taut, R Sánchez-González, E Navarro, A García, M Garcia-Sierra
pmc-11516682.description: IssueSchoolFood4Change (SF4C), an EU Horizon 2020 project in 12 EU countries, aims at making school meals healthier for children and the planet through innovative and sustainable food procurement, promotion of planetary health diets and cooking, and a Whole School Food Approach.

pmc-12549883.title: Fine-scale predictive modeling of Aedes mosquito abundance and dengue risk indicators using machine learning algorithms with microclimatic variables
pmc-12549883.creator: Nazri Che Dom, Nur Athen Mohd Hardy Abdullah, Rahmat Dapari, Siti Aekbal Salleh
pmc-12549883.description: Effective prediction of Aedes mosquito abundance and dengue risk indicators such as the Aedes Index (AI) and Dengue Positive Trap Index (DPTI) is essential for early intervention and targeted vector control. However, current models often rely on coarse regional data and fail to account for microclimatic variations, limiting their predictive accuracy in dengue hotspots.

pmc-13346715.title: Occupational Heat Exposure and Fertility Stress as Independent Factors of Low Semen Quality: A Multidimensional Analysis
pmc-13346715.creator: Ningning Han, Zhijuan Liu, Lijuan He, Rui Han
pmc-13346715.description: Semen quality is a key factor in male reproductive health. The multifactorial etiology of male infertility involves complex interactions between environmental exposures and psychological states. The “mind-body” interaction, specifically the synergistic impact of lifestyle, social support, and fertility stress on semen quality, remains underexplored. This cross-sectional study recruited 485 men from our hospital between May 2021 and April 2023.
